and do you o prince of the heavenly host, by the power of god cast into hell satan and all the evil spirits who wander through the world seeking the ruination of souls. amen thursdays: prayer for the sick and elderly father of goodness and love, hear our prayers for the sick, elderly, housebound members of our community and for all who are in need. amid mental and physical suffering may they find consolation in your healing presence and let us be a source of comfort for them. show your mercy to them as you close wounds, cure illness, make broken bodies whole and free downcast spirits. may these special people find lasting health and deliverance and so join us in thanking you for all your gifts. we ask this through jesus christ, your son, our lord, who healed those who believed. amen. fridays: “a prayer for vocations ” oh jesus, send labourers into your fields, which are awaiting holy apostles, saintly priests, heroic missionaries and dedicated sisters and brothers. enkindle in the hearts of men and women the spark of a vocation. grant that christian families may desire to give your church, helpers in the work of tomorrow. amen our next pope john paul meeting will take place on wednesday 21st october at 8pm in the parish office. everyone who is in 5th or 6th year, or aged 16 to 18 completing an apprenticeship or further education in the parish is welcome to join us! for more information contact catriona mcgovern -

we are accustomed to people presenting reality in whatever way suits their purposes. we see it in public life, online, and sometimes in ourselves. in sunday's gospel, jesus encounters people who are not interested in the truth. they want to trap him. but his answer about caesar's coin leads us to a much deeper question. the coin bears caesar's image. we bear god's image. our lives are not entirely of our own making. we have been given a dignity, a nature and a destiny. we discover something of their meaning in ordinary experience, especially when love makes claims upon us that we did not invent. christian faith helps us recognise the deeper significance of these experiences. we do not always respond as generously as we might. we are unfinished people. but our failures do not undo our belonging to god. we belong to him already. and through his grace, we are still becoming what he created us to be. church of the immaculate conception 200th anniversary: we will mark this significant milestone with a celebration mass on sunday 6th december at 11.00am. we would appreciate if you had any old photos, memories or recollections to share. photographs can be scanned and returned to the owner or copies can be forwarded to tempo@clogherparishes,.ie baptism or marriage: to arrange for these, please contact enniskillen parish office 6632-2075: monday to friday 10.30am to 2,30pm. bingo: bingo continues in st mary’s community centre each thursday night at 8.30pm with the usual prizes, £5,000 jackpot on game 10 *(on 44 calls or less) everyone welcome. choir practice for youth choir: each thursday evening 6.30 – 7.30pm.
